I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am p2 with $2111 and a pink monopoly of three hotels. The opponent has $216 and owns light blue, brown, and dark blue properties with hotels. I am at COMMUNITY_CHEST.

I am weighing the post-turn action options. Unmortgaging the railroads or Tennessee Avenue would be negative value. Trading cash would strengthen the opponent. Selling the pink hotels would reduce my rent income. I will keep both get-out-of-jail-free cards. My $2111 covers the Boardwalk hotel.

I rolled from St. Charles and landed on Community Chest at position 17. A roll of one would take me to Tennessee Avenue, which is mortgaged and mine. A roll of two would land on New York, mortgaged by the opponent.

The next roll would hit only safe spaces. All properties are mortgaged and the dark blues are too far away. I cannot collect rent or pass GO this turn.

The opponent is on Reading Railroad, which they own and have mortgaged. Their next roll could hit St. Charles, States, or Virginia for $750 to $900 each. They might also land on Chance or Community Chest.

The opponent has roughly a 39% chance of landing on one of my pink hotels next roll. If they hit St. Charles or States, they would need about $534 more cash. Selling their brown houses would return only $50 total.

I am calculating how much cash the opponent could raise by selling their light blue hotels. The standard Monopoly rule is to sell a hotel for half its purchase price, which would return about $150 per hotel. I need to verify whether this game engine follows that exact rule or handles hotel sales differently.

The opponent previously sold a single house on Baltic to pay a jail fine. They can liquidate individual buildings for cash. They could strip light blue and brown properties to raise about $1011, or sell dark blue houses to raise roughly $979. I am now calculating the exact cost of dark blue hotels.

Dark blue hotels cost $1200 each to build. Selling one returns about $600 if fully liquidated, or $100 with four houses remaining. Park Place hotel pays $1500 and Boardwalk hotel pays $2000. I can cover the Boardwalk rent with my current cash.

I can pay the Park Place hotel rent as well. I am ignoring conflicting estimates of how much cash selling my pink hotels would raise, and I will keep my current strategy.

If the opponent lands on one of my pink hotels, they would need roughly $534 more cash. Selling light blue hotels for half their cost would return only about $25 each and revert them to four houses. That would damage a dark-blue hotel and reduce their future rent income. The real danger remains landing on Park Place or Boardwalk.

I am now calculating the exact danger timeline. Landing on Tennessee Avenue would leave me 19 spaces from Park Place, which is unreachable in one roll. Landing on Marvin Gardens would leave me 8 spaces away, allowing a hit next turn. I can survive one Boardwalk hotel hit with my current cash, but multiple hits could deplete my reserves.

Light blue hotels pay $550 to $600 each. Reaching them from Community Chest would require a full loop around the board, so they are at least three turns away and I would collect $200 on the way. The dark blues are only 20 or 22 spaces away, so I could land there in two turns without passing GO.

I checked several two-roll paths to the dark blues. Even if I land on both Park Place and Boardwalk in consecutive turns, my $2111 cash would survive each hotel hit with a small remainder left over. The only way I could be forced into bankruptcy is if I hit another expense first.

All properties between Community Chest and Boardwalk are mortgaged. No rent is collectible in that stretch. The only risks are Chance cards, which could trigger repairs or send the opponent to Boardwalk. Luxury Tax is after Boardwalk, so I would hit the dark blue hotels first.

Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would cost $110 and yield only $25 in rent, so it is negative value. The opponent already owns St. James and New York, both mortgaged, which makes unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue a poor investment.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue would cost $99 for only $14 in rent. Trading it to the opponent would complete their orange monopoly. I will not sell my pink hotels because they are my main weapon against dark blue hotels. Trading cash would help them survive my pink hits and rebuild.

I am weighing a trade proposal. The opponent has almost no cash, so they cannot pay me much. They would likely reject any offer that strips their hotels. I could propose a trade and then receive another decision.

I am rejecting trade proposals that would help the opponent. Their dark blue hotels are untouchable. I cannot complete an orange set with Tennessee Avenue, so that property is not a priority.

I will keep my pink hotel trap and cash cushion. The opponent has a 14 in 36 chance of landing on one of my pink hotels next turn. If they hit Virginia Avenue for $900, they would need roughly $684 more cash. I am unsure how much cash they could raise by selling buildings, since the exact engine rules for hotel sales are unclear.

I calculated the exact cash the opponent could raise by selling buildings. Fully liquidating three light blue hotels and selling brown houses would return only about $500, plus their $216 cash, for a total of roughly $716. That is still below the $750 needed to cover a pink hotel hit. They would be forced to strip light blue hotels and damage a dark-blue hotel instead.

Almost all properties are already mortgaged, so the opponent cannot mortgage anything to raise cash. They must sell buildings instead, which guarantees they will damage a dark-blue hotel if they hit one of my pink hotels. I will keep my pink hotels and both Get Out of Jail Free cards.

Jail is a useful shelter in this endgame. I am now considering selling one of my pink hotels to increase my cash cushion, since the $111 margin against Boardwalk is too small to survive a general repairs hit.

Selling one pink hotel would return roughly $300, but the rent threat would drop to about $625–$750. That is still enough to cripple the opponent, since they can only raise about $716 by liquidating light blue hotels. The trade-off is unclear.

Four-house rent is $625, which the opponent can cover without selling dark-blue hotels. Hotel rent is $750, which they cannot cover without stripping dark-blue buildings. This confirms that keeping the hotels is essential to force them to damage their dark blues. I will not sell any hotels, unmortgage properties, or propose trades.
